A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiCE study. Their complete main text, equations, four figures, eighteen tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments on GMSC, Adult, and German Credit, plus Bayesian-network simulations and SPN-fit evaluations in Appendices F and G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original real-data experiments and appendix simulations, including counterfactual quality, runtime, statistical comparisons, and distribution-fit results.

M1.justification: The SPN-to-MIO formulation, input encoding, classifier constraints, counterfactual objectives, and LiCE variants are unchanged. Mentioning newer SPN-learning methods does not change the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GMSC, Adult, and German Credit, generate counterfactuals using asia, alarm, and win95pts simulations, and assess SPN fit on the same eight Bayesian networks.

E2.justification: DiCE, VAE, C-CHVAE, both FACE variants, PROPLACE, and the MIO comparator retain their participation in corresponding comparisons. Experiment-specific omissions are also unchanged. The added citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The five-fold evaluation, 500 factuals per real dataset, model architecture, preprocessing, metrics, top-ten candidate selection, and two-minute solver limit are unchanged. Appendices F.4 and G.4 retain their synthetic-data sample sizes and procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same SPN-approximation check, LiCE-variant comparisons, common-factual analysis, runtime analysis, true-distribution experiments, and SPN-fit evaluation. Relocated tables do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation reporting, five-seed synthetic procedures, Friedman tests, Nemenyi comparisons at alpha = 0.05, and correlation significance reporting are retained without changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries and findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains Adult LiCE (median) NLL of 12.9 ± 1.0. All four figures retain the same graphical results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–24, the log-sum-exp approximation bound, and the desiderata and histogram formulations in Appendices B and C are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an MIO formulation of SPNs and LiCE generation balancing plausibility with other counterfactual desiderata. Added references do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning computational cost, SPN approximation quality, baseline failures, and weaker results under common-success comparisons are retained. The future-work citation supplies an example within an existing proposal.

D1.justification: Implementation libraries, hyperparameters, hardware, computational-cost estimates, preprocessing instructions, and code/data access information remain unchanged. Appendix E.3 is displaced by layout changes rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v5 adds Laugel et al. (2023) on counterfactual diversity, Trapp et al. (2019) on Bayesian SPN learning, and Trapp et al. (2020) on structured Gaussian-process mixtures. These provide limited additional context without revising the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v5 makes brief wording additions in Sections 6–7 and Appendix B.2, adds citations, and edits the acknowledgment grant number. The section hierarchy and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned: Table 2 moves from page 8 to 9, Table 12 from 25 to 26, Tables 17–18 from 32 to 31, and Figure 4 from 31 to 32. Display designs, captions, and graphical content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added diversity survey and SPN references modestly improve scholarly context, particularly around the retained learning algorithm and future-work options. The method, empirical evidence, mathematical arguments, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited to literature coverage and contextual clarity.
